item.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
item.description: arXiv:2611.05423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $\chi(G)\le\max\{\omega(G),\Delta(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours. We estimate the number of stars that can be chosen after the clique colours have been exposed, while keeping their endpoint set fixed. A common exponential-moment argument reduces intervals of packing sizes to endpoint comparisons. More detailed neighbourhood estimates handle the remaining vertices. The final probability inequalities are verified by directed rational and interval arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Lizhong Chen

item.title: Extremal even-cycle-free subgraphs of the $k$-ary $n$-cube
item.description: arXiv:2611.05433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is said to be $H$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Tur\'{a}n number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. For any integer $\ell\geq 2$, let $C_{2\ell}$ denote the even cycle of length $2\ell$. So far, extensive studies of the generalized Tur\'{a}n number for the hypercube $Q_{n}$ have been conducted. The $k$-ary $n$-cube is an important family of graphs with many favorable properties, such as regularity and vertex-transitivity. It generalizes the hypercube and reduces to the hypercube when $k=2$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(Q^{k}_{n}, C_{2\ell})$ of $Q^{k}_{n}$ for all even integers $k\geq 4$ and integers $\ell\geq 2$, generalizing the result for $Q_{n}$ [J. Graph Theory 16 (1992) 273-286] from $k=2$ to $k\geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Li Zhao, Yu-Qi Li

item.title: Stabiliser codes over prime fields as weighted graphs and as quantum sets of lines
item.description: arXiv:2611.05489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We further develop the theory of quantum stabiliser codes and its links with graph theory and finite geometry. We prove that an [[n,k,d]]_p stabiliser code over a finite field with p elements, p prime, gives rise to a graph on n-k vertices together with two disjoint independent sets of size k. Its edges are weighted with elements of a finite field of size p. If k=0, such codes are known as graph states. Second, we view stabiliser codes as so-called quantum sets of lines in projective space, allowing us to determined their minimum distance geometrically. We describe two geometrical operations to obtain new quantum sets of lines from given quantum sets of lines. As an application, we list the number of stabiliser codes up to equivalence, for given small parameters.
item.dc:creator: Simeon Ball, G\"ulizar G\"unay, Robin Simoens, Ricard Vilar

item.title: Hamilton cycles in bicirculants with non-coprime connection sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.05531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A bicirculant is a regular graph that admits an automorphism having two vertex-orbits of the same size. A bicirculant can be described as follows. Given an integer $m \ge 1$ and sets $R, S, T \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_m$ such that $R=-R$, $T=-T$, $0 \not\in R \cup T$ and $0 \in S$, the graph $B(m;R,S,T)$ has vertex set $V=\{u_0,\dots,u_{m-1},v_0,\dots,v_{m-1}\}$ and edge set $E=\{u_iu_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in R\} \cup \{v_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in T\} \cup \{u_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in S\}.$ Some of the well known bicirculants include the generalized Petersen graphs and Cayley graphs of dihedral groups. In 1983, Brian Alspach proved that the only non-hamiltonian generalized Petersen graphs are $G(m,2)$ where $m \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. In a recent paper we conjectured that this is the only exception among regular connected bicirculants of degree at least two, and we have verified the conjecture for bicirculants with $|S|\le 3$. Results of Alspach, Chen and Dean imply that the conjecture also holds for all bicirculants with $m$ even and $\gcd(m,S)=1$. In this paper, we show that the conjecture holds for all bicirculants with $|S| \geq 4$ and $\gcd(m,S)>1$ such that $R\cup T$ contains an element that is not coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$ and, if $m$ is odd, is also not divisibile by $\gcd(m, S)$ or $R \cap T$ contains an element that is coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$.
item.dc:creator: Simona Bonvicini, Toma\v{z} Pisanski, Arjana \v{Z}itnik

item.title: Non-redundant Independence Atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.05568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Independence atom is a key concept in relational database theory. In the present paper, we prove that the maximum possible size of a non-redundant set of independence atoms on $n$ attributes is asymptotically $(1+o(1))\binom{n}{\floor{n/2}}$. It turns out that this problem is closely related to two extremal set theory problems, the Katona-Tarj\'an question on ``V''-free families of subsets of $[n]$ for the lower bound, and Kleitman's bound on union-free families for the upper bound.
item.dc:creator: Attila Sali, Jun Yan

item.title: Almost All 3-uniform Hypergraphs are Class 1
item.description: arXiv:2611.05622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The chromatic index $\chi'(H)$ of a hypergraph $H$ is the smallest number of colors needed to color its edges so that no two adjacent edges share the same color. The chromatic index is trivially bounded below by the maximum degree $\Delta(H)$, and when $\chi'(H)= \Delta(H)$, we say that $H$ is Class 1. It is well known that almost every 2-graph is Class 1, and we extend this result to 3-graphs. We show for $n^{-2/3-1/200}\leq p \leq 0.99$ that the $3$-uniform binomial random hypergraph $H\sim H_{n,p}^{(3)}$ is Class 1 with high probability. We also show that this result doesn't hold for uniformities above $3$. For a broad range of $p$, when $k \geq 4$ and $k \nmid n$, the hypergraph $H \sim H_{n,p}^{(k)}$ is with high probability not Class 1.
item.dc:creator: Arnab Chaterjee, Asaf Ferber, Marcelo Sales, Mason Shurman

item.title: On Diameter Graphs Problems: A proof of Brass's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.05631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The diameter graph of a finite set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ has vertex set $S$ and two points are adjacent when their distance equals $\operatorname{diam} S$. In this paper we study the following question: given $k$ and $d$, is there a constant $c=c(k,d)$ such that from every finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ one can remove at most $c$ points so that the subgraph of the diameter graph induced by the remaining points is $k$-colorable? Brass conjectured that such a constant exists for $d=3$ and $k=3$. We prove this conjecture by showing that at most one point needs to be removed. We also answer a question of Dol'nikov, showing that for every positive integer $m$, there exist a finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ in which every subset of smaller diameter has less than $(|S|-m)/2$ points.
item.dc:creator: Gyivan Lopez-Campos

item.title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2611.05634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Q_p^d$ be the random subgraph of the $d$-dimensional binary hypercube obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. A long-standing folklore conjecture states that the emergence of the giant component in $Q_p^d$, at $p\approx 1/d$, is accompanied by the emergence of cycles of linear length. We confirm this conjecture and determine the order of the longest cycle near the phase transition. Specifically, for every sufficiently small constant $\varepsilon>0$, we show that if $p=(1+\varepsilon)/d$, then with high probability the longest cycle of $Q_p^d$ has length $\Theta(\varepsilon^2 2^d)$. The dependence on $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to constant factors.
item.dc:creator: Michael Anastos

item.title: Orthogonal polynomials on two or more intervals: the Sprugnoli context
item.description: arXiv:2611.05673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how the group of Sprugnoli arrays on three elements can be used to define families of polynomials that are orthogonal on two intervals, and we indicate how the group can be extended in the hierarchy of Sprugnoli groups to yield families of orthogonal polynomials with more complex supports. In particular, we examine the defining three term recurrences and the Jacobi matrices of these families of orthogonal polynomials, while detailing the Sprugnoli matrix structure of the coefficient matrices of the polynomial families. We also consider integral representations of the principal moments on the defining intervals. Sprugnoli arrays are shown to relate to periodic recurrences where the parameters remain cyclically constant.
item.dc:creator: Paul Barry

item.title: A toric approach to social choice theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.05745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper initiates a systematic study of objects in convex geometry and toric algebraic geometry arising from status quo systems in social choice theory. Our main application is to classify all cones arising from a large class of status quo systems that are smooth or simplicial.
item.dc:creator: Ata Poyraz Turna, Ben Y. Wormleighton

item.title: Cyclotomic factorization and fixed-point insertion in colored permutation groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.05848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend cyclotomic Euler--Mahonian factorization to colored permutation groups for two inversion statistics: Biagioli--Zeng length and the inversion number of the underlying unsigned permutation. At a primitive $m$th root and rank $n=mk+i$, each normalized enumerator is a Hadamard product of a rank-$i$ colored enumerator and a weighted rank-$k$ type-B enumerator. Separate color variables are retained. The type-B factors agree for the two statistics, yielding equidistribution modulo the rank jointly with descent number, major index and negative-entry number. We also determine their exact changes under positive fixed-point insertion and obtain rational kernels retaining descent and major index. These kernels mark arbitrary fixed-point numbers and give derangement expansions at every inversion weight. Signed specializations recover type-A and type-B identities and give colored flag-major refinements. Inverse statistics and color-sum subgroups admit related insertion formulas.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Zeng

item.title: A Complete Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly-extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1, k, q-k+2]_q$. We give a complete characterization of when its codewords of a fixed weight form $q$-ary 2-designs. The main ingredient is an exact criterion showing that the number of $r$-subsets of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$ with a prescribed product is independent of that product if and only if $\gcd(r, q-1)=1$. Applying this criterion to the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$, we prove that they form a $q$-ary 2-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$. We further establish a propagation result for MDS codes showing that the $q$-ary 2-design property at minimum weight implies the same property at every nonzero weight. Consequently, $\mathcal{C}_k$ holds $q$-ary 2-designs at all nonzero weights if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$.
item.dc:creator: Xinghao Wu, Junling Zhou

item.title: An Asymptotic for E. P. Stein Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.05898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Epstein's put-or-take-a-square game is an impartial combinatorial game in which a player may, in each turn, add or subtract the largest square not exceeding the current integer. We study E. P. Stein numbers, the positions from which both legal moves lead directly to positive squares, and prove the following asymptotic formula for the counting function $S_2(X)$ of these positions: \[ S_2(X)=\frac{1}{\pi^2}X^{1/4}\log X+O(X^{1/4}). \]
item.dc:creator: Cameron Rampell

item.title: One-Vertex Lifts of Looped Circle Graphs: Obstructions and Interlace Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.05961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of a looped simple graph over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and let $t=\operatorname{diag} M$. We study the one-vertex lift with adjacency matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}M+tt^T&t\\t^T&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. A looped circle graph is called stable if its lift is a circle graph. We prove that stability is equivalent to the existence of a pseudo-orientable bouquet realizing the given looped circle graph. We then obtain a finite excluded toggle-minor characterization by applying two rooted constructions to the known excluded pivot-minors for circle graphs. An exact enumeration yields $22$ minimal toggle-equivalence classes: one of order $5$, twelve of order $6$, and nine of order $7$. The enumeration is accompanied by independently checkable linear-algebra and minor certificates. Finally, we prove $q(G^\dagger;y)=yq(G;y)$ for the vertex-nullity interlace polynomial of every looped simple graph, and derive quasi-tree counting and real determinant formulas.
item.dc:creator: Qingying Deng, Yexiang Yan

item.title: Exact $3$-Adic Periods of Symmetric Dellac Numbers and Their Polynomial Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The odd and even symmetric Dellac numbers are the specializations $a_n=f_n(0)$ and $e_n=f_n(1)$ of the Randrianarivony--Zeng family $f_n(s)=2^{-n}D_n(s)$. Using a finite Stieltjes-fraction truncation, we establish the sharp congruence $v_3(a_n)=1$ for $n\ge2$ and obtain explicit congruences modulo $81$ for both sequences. We also establish universal eventual periodicity modulo arbitrary positive integers. For every integer $s\ge0$ and $k\ge1$, we give and analyse formulas for the \emph{least} eventual period of $f_n(s)$ modulo $3^k$ and its \emph{least starting index}. The period is governed by five linear factors in $s$; the onset follows a nine-class formula modulo $9$. In particular, for $k\ge3$ the even symmetric Dellac period is three times the odd period and begins one index earlier. The proofs combine a finite Stieltjes-fraction certificate, a graded $3$-adic pole expansion, and an explicit finite top-degree certificate over $\F_3$. Finite integer-arithmetic checks supplement the proofs. We also record the connection with the type-$B$ homogenized Linial arrangement.
item.dc:creator: Tony Newton, Jiang Zeng

item.title: Coherent configuration on 3-uniform hypergraph over strongly regular graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.05980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates coherent configurations on 3-uniform hypergraphs constructed from strongly regular graphs. We establish that the hypergraph preserves the automorphism group of the original graph and induces a nonhomogeneous Schurian coherent configuration. Using the case of Petersen graph, we obtain a configuration with two fibers and thirteen basic relations. We further determine their valencies and nonzero intersection numbers, together with the corresponding adjacency matrix multiplication identities.
item.dc:creator: Fajri Maulana

item.title: Finiteness of Non-decomposable Critically Frustrated Signed Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A signed graph $(G,\sigma)$ is a graph $G$ with a signature $\sigma$ labeling each edge with a positive or negative sign. Two signatures of $G$ are switching equivalent if one is obtained from the other by sequentially changing the signs of all edges in an edge-cut. The frustration index of a signed graph $(G, \sigma)$ is the minimum number of negative edges among all signatures switching equivalent to $\sigma$. A signed graph is critically $k$-frustrated if it has frustration index $k$, and the removal of any edge decreases its frustration index. A critically $k$-frustrated signed graph is prime if it is irreducible and contains no two edge-disjoint negative cycles. Steffen and Naserasr et al. asked if there are only finitely many prime critically $k$-frustrated signed graphs for any positive integer $k$. The cases $k\leq 3$ were proved to be true by Cappello et al., and later, the cases $k=4$ and $5$ were verified by Z. Wang. In this paper, the author proves the conjecture by a topological argument.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqian Wang

item.title: On the Cameron-Praeger conjecture for Steiner 6-designs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A long-standing and far-reaching conjecture of Cameron and Praeger (1993) asserts that no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs exist. Huber (2010) reduced the Steiner case ($\lambda=1$) to a single infinite family of possible exceptions, where the automorphism group is $G=\PGaL(2,p^e)$ acting on the points of the projective line, with $p\in\{2,3\}$ and $e$ an odd prime power. In this paper, we resolve this final case. By combining orbit-stabiliser analysis for the action of specific involutions in $\PGaL(2,p^e)$ with the modular arithmetic constraints derived from the design parameters, we prove that no such Steiner 6-designs can exist for any admissible $q$. This completes the proof that the Cameron-Praeger conjecture is true for the important case of non-trivial Steiner 6-designs.
item.dc:creator: Ximin Wang, Zheng Huang, Weijun Liu

item.title: Geodesic Transversal of Hypercube and Butterfly networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.06107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A geodesic $P$ of a connected graph $G(V,E)$ is called a maximal geodesic if there exists no geodesic $P'$ in $G$ that contains $P$ as its sub-path. The geodesic transversal problem determines a subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ such that every possible maximal geodesic of $G$ includes at least one vertex of $S$. Such a set with minimum number of elements is called a gt-set and its cardinality is the gt-number of $G$. In this paper, we establish a general result, called the Geodesic Transversal lemma which provides a lower bound for the gt-number of an arbitrary graph $G$ in terms of the gt-number of its induced subgraphs. Using this lemma, we determine the gt-number of Butterfly and Hypercube networks.
item.dc:creator: R. Prabha, B. Sandhiya, Paul Manuel

item.title: Highly connected uniquely $k$-linked digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extending a result of Thomassen, we prove that for every choice of positive integers $K\geq k$ there exist a $K$-strong digraph which has two disjoint sets $S,T$ each of size $k$ so that the only linkage from $S$ to $T$ in $D$ is the one whose existence follows from Menger's theorem.
item.dc:creator: J{\o}rgen Bang-Jensen

item.title: Constructing Cospectral Hypergraphs Using Adjacency Preserving Permutations
item.description: arXiv:2611.06199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we use permutations of the vertices of hypergraphs that preserve their adjacency matrices defined in banerjee 2021. These permutations form a group which lies between the automorphism group and the full symmetric group $S_n$ where $n$ is the number of vertices. Using elements from that group which are not automorphisms, we construct cospectral non-isomorphic hypergraphs. We use hypergraph structure coming from finite projective planes to show existence of infinitely many families of such hypergraphs. Also this method is very specific to uniform hypergraphs with uniformity greater than or equal to 3, i.e not applicable to graphs.
item.dc:creator: Arpita Das, Debjit Ghosal

item.title: Small 5-chromatic unit-distance graphs in disks of radius 3/2, 5/4 and 23/20
item.description: arXiv:2611.06269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give three explicit unit-distance graphs in the plane with chromatic number 5 whose vertices lie in small disks: a graph with 773 vertices inside an open disk of radius 3/2, one with 5713 vertices inside an open disk of radius 5/4, and one with 8168 vertices inside an open disk of radius 23/20. The smallest examples previously reported for these radii have 11725, 11725 and 31171 vertices. All coordinates are exact elements of Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11). In each case 5-chromaticity is certified by an explicit 5-colouring and a DRAT proof that no 4-colouring exists. The 773-vertex graph is vertex-critical.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Shukla

item.title: On generalized $k$-token graphs with distinguishable tokens and a maximum capacity of $s$ tokens per vertex
item.description: arXiv:2611.06275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supertoken graphs \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\), also known as generalized token graphs, model configurations of \(k\) distinguishable tokens on a graph \(G\), with at most \(s\) tokens at each vertex. We study structural and metric properties of these graphs in terms of the base graph. For regular \(G\), we characterize when \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\) is regular. We show that bipartiteness is inherited from \(G\) and characterize it for complete base graphs. For \(s\ge2\), we characterize connectedness and show that \(t\)-vertex-connectivity of \(G\) implies \(t\)-vertex-connectivity of the supertoken graph. We obtain exact diameter formulas in several regimes, including complete graphs and stars, and derive lower bounds and a conjectured formula for odd cycles. We also determine the clique number, give bounds and equality conditions for the chromatic number, and characterize planarity for complete base graphs.
item.dc:creator: Yiting Cai, Cristina Dalf\'o, Blas Fern\'andez, Miquel \`Angel Fiol

item.title: Hamiltonicity and cycle factors in k-quasi-transitive digraphs of large diameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.06310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A digraph is $k$-quasi-transitive if the endpoints of every directed path of length $k$ are adjacent. In this paper, we prove that every strong non-bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian when $k\ge7$ is odd. Moreover, combined with the known even case, for $k\ge6$, we also prove that a strong bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it has a cycle factor. These answer two problems posed by Alva-Samos and Hern\'andez-Cruz affirmatively [Journal of Graph Theory \textbf{96} (2021) 310--325].
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang, Panpan Cheng

item.title: Four-colour counterexamples for monochromatic path partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.06362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1989, Gy\'arf\'as conjectured that the vertex set of every $r$-edge-coloured complete graph can be partitioned into at most $r$ monochromatic paths. The case $r=2$ follows from a theorem of Gerencs\'er and Gy\'arf\'as, and Pokrovskiy proved the conjecture for $r=3$. Recently, Li and Wang disproved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $r$, leaving open the smallest number of colours for which it fails. We show that this number is four. For every integer $n\geq118$, we construct a four-edge-colouring of $K_n$ in which every monochromatic path partition contains at least five paths. We also construct, for every integer $n\geq60$, a four-edge-colouring of $K_{n,n}$ in which every monochromatic path partition contains at least eight paths, disproving Pokrovskiy's conjectured bound $2r-1$ for balanced complete bipartite graphs when $r=4$.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Liu, Chuanshu Wu

item.title: On Partitions with Constant-Sum Gap Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.06417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study \emph{constant-sum gap partitions}: for a fixed nonnegative integer $C$, these are partitions $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k)$ whose successive differences $d_i=\lambda_{i+1}-\lambda_i$ satisfy $d_i+d_{k-i}=C$ for all valid $i$. We derive the generating function for this family, treating partitions of odd and even length separately, and compute it explicitly for $C=0, 1,2,3,4$. We then construct explicit bijections between constant-sum gap partitions with $2m+1$, respectively $2m$, parts and partitions into odd, respectively even, parts in which parts below the largest part have bounded multiplicity, together with an exact weight relation between a partition and its image. Finally, we give a geometric characterization of constant-sum gap partitions in terms of their Ferrers diagrams: removing a prescribed, linearly growing number of cells from each row renders the diagram symmetric about its middle row, for both the odd- and even-length cases.
item.dc:creator: Halime \"Omr\"uuzun Seyrek

item.title: Scopes arrangements and product formulas
item.description: arXiv:2611.06419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop normalized abacus combinatorics for affine type \(C\). We also give explicit product formulas for the number of Scopes classes at every level and every positive depth in affine types \(A\) and \(C\).
item.dc:creator: Huang Lin, Tao Qin

item.title: Cycles in Regular Multipartite Tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2611.06468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study balanced cycles in regular multipartite tournaments. A cycle in a $c$-partite tournament is $k$-balanced if it contains exactly $k$ vertices from each partite class. We prove that there exists an absolute integer $r_0$ such that every regular $c$-partite tournament with each partite class size of $r\ge r_0$ contains a $k$-balanced cycle for every $1\le k\le r$ when $c=3$ or $c\ge5$, and for every $2\le k\le r$ when $c=4$. In particular, our result confirms three conjectures of Volkmann and Winzen for large regular multipartite tournaments. We also confirm Yeo's conjecture on the existence of $(p,q)$-cycle factors for large regular $c$-partite tournaments $G$ with $c\ge4$, where a $(p,q)$-cycle factor is a pair of vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $p$ and $q$ spanning $G$.
item.dc:creator: Yufei Chang, Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei, Jin Yan

item.title: How many sorted projections determine n points in k dimensions?
item.description: arXiv:2611.06470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers. How many directions are needed for these projections to determine every multiset of $n$ points? Two simple bounds are known in every dimension: more than $(k-1)\log_2 n$ directions are always needed, and $(k-1)n+1$ directions in general position always suffice. In the plane much more is known: Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron showed that almost every choice of $O(\log n \log\log n)$ directions suffices. Whether anything similar holds in higher dimensions was left open by Dym, Wellershoff, Tsoukanis, Levy and Balan. We observe that two lemmas of Hair and Sahai, proved for list recovery of random linear codes, answer that question, and by tightening their argument we show that in every dimension almost every choice of $(4k-2)\ln(2n)\ln(k\log_2 2n)+k+1$ directions suffices. For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.78^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Gorham Lester, Raymond Hau S{\o}rensen

item.title: A characterization of a family of integral Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. In our earlier work, we proved that the quasi-strongly regular Cayley graph $\Gamma_H(G)$ is integral whenever $H$ is normal in $G$, and raised the question of whether the converse also holds. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively. We prove that if $\Gamma_H(G)$ is integral, then $H$ must be a normal subgroup of $G$. Consequently, $\Gamma_H(G)$ is integral if and only if $H\lhd G$. Our proof uses the irreducible representations of $G$ and the dimensions of their $H$-fixed subspaces. For a non-normal subgroup $H$, we construct a two-dimensional invariant subspace of a suitable representation operator and show that the corresponding eigenvalues are irrational.
item.dc:creator: Sauvik Poddar, Sucharita Biswas

item.title: Baxter Structures and the Odd-Even Enumeration of Red-Blue Motzkin Paths
item.description: arXiv:2611.06599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Motzkin paths satisfying the red-blue rule introduced by Wu, Eu, Ku and Shih. We answer their Question 8.5 and exhibit two new Baxter structures. Let $\mathcal M_m$ denote the set of such paths of length $m$ and $a_m=|\mathcal M_m|$. We give a combinatorial proof of \[ a_{2n-1}=\mathrm{A005802}(n),\qquad a_{2n}=\mathrm{A216947}(n) \qquad (n\geq 1). \] For the odd subsequence, we construct a bijection with $1234$-avoiding permutations which sends the initial up and terminal down runs to the initial decreasing runs of a permutation and its inverse. The boundary correspondence arising from this bijection further identifies red-blue Motzkin paths of length $2n$ with $1234$-avoiding permutations of length $n+1$ in which $1$ occurs to the left of $2$. We establish parallel binomial decompositions of this restricted permutation class and of $2$-colored noncrossing set partitions. The two decompositions have the same binomial coefficients, and their respective cores are explicitly in bijection with non-intersecting triples of lattice paths, a classical Baxter family. This establishes the even identity. Moreover, we construct a second bijection between odd-length red-blue Motzkin paths and $1234$-avoiding permutations. Under this bijection, splitting a path at its ground-level blue horizontal steps corresponds to the skew decomposition of the associated permutation.
item.dc:creator: Joanna N. Chen

item.title: Non-induced inherent graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Concepts of avoidable paths and inherent two-rooted graphs were recently introduced for the case of induced subgraphs. In this paper, we translate this framework to the setting of not necessarily induced (NNI) subgraphs, where the structural constraints, as well as conclusions, are significantly relaxed. We develop a new sufficient condition for inherence, and use it to provide complete characterizations of inherent two-rooted paths and forks. We show that for these families, the obvious necessary condition for inherence from the induced case is sufficient in the NNI setting. To complement these results, we introduce two general methods for proving non-inherence and apply them to demonstrate the non-inherence of several classes of two-rooted trees. Keywords: subgraph, two-rooted graph, two-rooted tree, avoidable two-rooted graph, inherent two-rooted graph
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Gurvich, Matja\v{z} Krnc, Martin Milani\v{c}, Mikhail Vyalyi

item.title: Polylogarithmic bound for the Gy\'arf\'as-Sumner conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.06699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Gy\'arf\'as-Sumner conjecture asserts that for any fixed forest $F$, any graph $G$ not containing $F$ as an induced subgraph, with bounded clique number $\omega(G)$, has bounded chromatic number $\chi(G)$. Recently, Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour proved that every such graph has chromatic number at most $|G|^{o(1)}$. We improve this bound to a polylogarithmic one $(\log |G|)^{O(1)}$.
item.dc:creator: Martin Bierbaumer, Matija Buci\'c

item.title: Counting graphs admitting a strictly matched involution
item.description: arXiv:2611.06703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study graphs admitting a strictly matched involution, i.e., graphs for which a strictly matched involution exists. A strictly matched involution of a graph $G$ is a self-inverse graph automorphism $f$ with the properties that the fixed point set of $f$ induces a complete subgraph in $G$ and, for the vertices that are no fixed points, every vertex is connected to its image under $f$ by an edge. Andres, Huggan, Mc Inerney, and Nowakowski (2019) determined upper and lower bounds for the number $A(n)$ of graphs admitting a strictly matched involution on $n$ vertices. We improve the upper bound and we compute the exact values for the number $A(n)$ for all $n\leq11$. Furthermore, we use combinatorial enumeration techniques and a decomposition lemma to determine the number $C(n,m)$ of graphs admitting a strictly matched involution with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges for several infinite classes of pairs $(n,m)$.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Dominique Andres, Igor Re\v{z}an

item.title: A family of symmetric counterexamples to the bent sum decomposition conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.06744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide an infinite family of counterexamples to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions. The conjecture states that every Boolean function in an even number of variables $n$ of algebraic degree at most $n/2$ can be written as the sum of two bent functions. We show that for every $n=2^k\geq 8$, the symmetric function $F_n=1+\sigma_2+\sigma_4+\sigma_6+\cdots+\sigma_{n/2}$ has degree $n/2$ and cannot be written as a sum of at most two bent functions. Here $\sigma_j$ is the elementary symmetric Boolean polynomial of degree $j$. Furthermore, we show that the eight-variable member of this family can be represented as the sum of exactly three bent functions. Using the connection between bent-sum decompositions and derivatives of bent functions, we also obtain an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions that cannot be derivatives of bent functions.
item.dc:creator: M\'at\'e R\'obert Kepes, Anita Kercs\'o-Moln\'ar, Viczi\'an Andr\'as

item.title: The Exact Number of Pentagons in Book-Free Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $B_k$ denote the book consisting of $k$ triangles sharing a common edge. We prove that there exist absolute constants $\rho>0$ and $N$ such that, for every pair of integers $n,k$ with $n\ge N$ and $2\le k\le \rho n$, writing $n=5q+r$ with $0\le r<5$, \[ \operatorname{ex}(n,C_5,B_k)=q^{\,5-r}(q+1)^r, \] with the balanced complete $C_5$-blow-ups as the only extremal graphs. The linear order of this range is best possible since for all sufficiently large $n$, the formula fails whenever $k\ge0.14n$.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Hu

item.title: Proof of two conjectures on the log-concavity of partition ranks and cranks
item.description: arXiv:2611.06757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang proved that the crank sequence $(M(m,n))_{|m|\le n-1}$ is unimodal for every $n\ge44$. Bringmann, Man, and Rolen subsequently established the unimodality of the rank sequence $(N(m,n))_{|m|\le n-2}$ for every $n\ge39$. Ji and Zang also conjectured that $(M(m,n))_{|m|\le n-71}$ is log-concave for every $n\ge72$, and that $(N(m,n))_{|m|\le n-72}$ is log-concave for every $n\ge73$. In this paper, we prove both conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Jianxi Mao, Wenle Shi, Bao-Xuan Zhu

item.title: Largest Sperner families with bounded VC-dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.06860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conjecture of Frankl proposed in the 1980s states that for $n\ge2d$, every Sperner family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ of VC-dimension at most $d$ has at most $\binom{n}{d}$ members. We prove this conjecture for every fixed $d$ and large $n$, and show that equality holds only when $\mathcal{F}$ is $\binom{[n]}{d}$ or $\binom{[n]}{n-d}$.
item.dc:creator: Gennian Ge, Hanyu Wang, Zixiang Xu, Yixuan Zhang

item.title: Off-Diagonal Induced Ramsey Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.06886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given graphs $F$ and $H$, the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H)$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that every red-blue colouring of $E(G)$ contains either a blue induced copy of $F$ or a red induced copy of $H$. A conjecture of Kohayakawa, Pr\"omel and R\"odl asserts that, for every fixed graph $F$, this number is polynomial in $v(H)$. We prove this conjecture, showing that there is an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $$r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H) \leq v(H)^{Cv(F)^2}$$ for all graphs $F$ and $H$. The proof combines a variant of a random geometric construction of Kohayakawa, Pr\"omel and R\"odl with the hypergraph container method.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Andrades, Marcelo Campos, Rafael Filipe, Anastasiia Kats

item.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
item.description: arXiv:2610.29898v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Haussler's covering lemma (JCTA 1995) gives the sharp $(C/\delta)^d$ metric-entropy bound for binary VC classes under normalized $\ell_1$ distance. We prove a sharp global dynamic analogue for bounded real-valued classes in normalized $\ell_p$, for every $1\le p<\infty$. Writing $d=\operatorname{sfat}_{\varepsilon/32}(\mathcal F)$, we obtain a global dynamic cover of size at most $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ for every horizon and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Here a single family of deterministic causal experts, fixed independently of the instance sequence, covers every target on every sequence. For $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, a matching worst-case lower bound $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$ holds already for binary classes on one fixed sequence, even with real-valued experts. The constants are universal, independent of $p$. For $p=2$, this resolves the horizon-independent sequential $\ell_2$ covering problem of Rakhlin, Sridharan, and Tewari (PTRF 2015) in a stronger global form. For $p=1$, it gives the sharp $(C/\delta)^{\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal H)}$ global dynamic covering bound for binary classes, resolving questions of Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Dagan, Moran, Naor, and Yogev (STOC 2021) and Malliaris and Moran (Trans. AMS 2024). Our proof combines rank-decreasing correction schedules and accurate sampled prefixes with exact continuations after target identification. Shared-parent routing distributes these continuations among eligible prefixes, eliminating the logarithmic overhead.
item.dc:creator: Shihao Shao, Dacheng Tao

item.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.39242v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.
item.dc:creator: Kuijun Liu, Feng Luo, Yanwen Luo, Zhenghao Rao

item.title: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2611.00082v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The 2-switch operation for reducing the number of short cycles in Tanner graphs of LDPC codes has been utilized in some works. If this operation is appropriately applied to a 2-induced matching in a bipartite graph, then it surely preserves the bipartiteness of the graph. With a 2-induced matching, we have only one choice for applying this type of change to the graph. Using 3-induced matchings creates more potential and flexibility to apply certain changes to the Tanner graph. We present a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a 3-induced matching in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6. A 3-induced matching helps us to have more choices for applying a change to a bipartite graph while surely preserving the bipartiteness of the graph and keeping the degree sequences unchanged. Among all changes that we consider, we select the best change for reducing the number of cycles of length 6. The eigenvalues of subgraphs are used to reach a 3-induced matching, and a condition in some steps can be checked to ensure that the subgraph has at least one 3-induced matching. We present some numerical results regarding the steps at which the condition that guarantees the existence of a 3-induced matching is checked.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Eshraghi Dehaghani, Sara Saeedi Madani, Dariush Kiani

item.title: Isosceles sets in Euclidean spaces of dimension nine to twenty-two
item.description: arXiv:2611.05421v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erd\H{o}s asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The answer was known for $d\le 8$, the last cases being due to Ionin. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le 21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre, and the number $\binom d2+3$ is attained. The proof combines Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets, for which we give a short self-contained proof (the key step is a special case of Gallai's theorem on edge colourings without rainbow triangles), with the recent determination of the maximum two-distance sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $9\le d\le22$ and with the known maximum sizes of spherical two-distance sets. In dimension nine this gives only $\mathrm{iso}(9)\le47$, and the exact value $46$ requires an additional argument about eight-dimensional two-distance sets with at least $44$ points. We also show that $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}$, where $g(23)$ is the largest size of a two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$, so that $278\le\mathrm{iso}(23)\le575$.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjun Yi

item.title: On the most informative Boolean function under noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.05430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a uniform random bit string and $Y$ be obtained by flipping each bit of $X$ independently with probability $p$. Let $C$ be a random bit obtained as a function of $Y$. We show that $\mathbf{I}(C:X)\le \mathbf{I}(Y_1:X)$ for all $p\in[0,1]$, which resolves a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013.
item.dc:creator: Dimiter Kramer, Mert Saglam

item.title: Quantum error correcting codes from quiver moduli: Grassmannians, cyclic monodromy, and argyle collision divisors
item.description: arXiv:2611.05526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on aspects of a recent diagrammatic field-theory programme for quantum error correction put forward by the first-named author (arXiv:2607.08911), we construct exact finite-dimensional codes from twisted cyclic and argyle quiver moduli on the projective line. A regular fibre of the node-labelled cyclic Hitchin map records the ways to distribute simple spectral zeroes among the arrows with prescribed degrees. The Hilbert space spanned by these allocations is a Young permutation module. Root monodromy acts on its Specht factors and leaves their multiplicity spaces noiseless. Resetting the Specht factor therefore recovers the encoded state for every channel in the monodromy noise model. We prove that the largest Kostka multiplicity is the optimal dimension of a subspace code correcting the full monodromy algebra, even among codes spanning several isotypic blocks. Quantizing an argyle master space recovers the cyclic sheet space as a weight sector of a tensor power, with the identification preserving monodromy. For the balanced three-cycle with $t$ zeroes per arrow, the multiplicity of a partition $(a,b,c)$ of $3t$ is $1+\min(a-b,b-c)$. The optimal logical dimension is thus $t+1$, attained uniquely by the block indexed by $(2t,t)$. At $t=1$ we give explicit codewords for a qubit on six sheets. The commuting right action generates its full logical algebra, yielding errors outside the monodromy model that leave the measured footprint statistics unchanged yet require different recoveries. We also compute collision-parity ranks, give a higher-rank Grassmannian example, and derive a conditional criterion for recovery across splitting types.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rayan, Evan Sundbo

item.title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.05532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the graph shotgun assembly problem in the labeled lattice model, as introduced by Mossel and Ross (2019). We start with a $d$-dimensional lattice of length $n$, where the color of each vertex is sampled i.i.d. from a distribution $\pi$. Then, we ask whether it is possible to reconstruct the coloring of the lattice given the coloring of each subgrid of length $k$. While previous work by Ding and Liu (2023) and Demidovich, Panichkin, and Zhukovskii (2023) identified the reconstruction threshold when $\pi$ is uniform, we examine the non-uniform case. This paper establishes a sufficient condition for the impossibility of reconstruction for $d \geq 2$ using information-theoretic arguments. Our negative result matches the known threshold in the uniform case.
item.dc:creator: Julia Gaudio, Charlie K. Guan, Andrew Jin

item.title: Partitions with designated summands: $k$-tuples and their congruences
item.description: arXiv:2611.05623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A_k(n)$ and $B_k(n)$ be the numbers of ordered $k$-tuples of partitions with designated summands, respectively with designated summands and all parts odd, of total size $n$. Using an exact description of the generating function of designated partitions after a $3$-dissection, we classify for every $e$ the values of $k$ for which $A_k(3n+2)$ is divisible by $3^e$: this happens exactly when $k\equiv0$ or $-5\pmod{3^e}$ if $e\le4$, and when $3^e\mid k$ if $e\ge5$. We obtain the corresponding exact $3$-adic and several $2$-adic results for $B_k$ and for $A_k$ along the progressions $4n+3$, a recursion for the classes $3^b(3n+s)$, and for $k=2$ the congruences $A_2(12n+10)\equiv 27f_1^4f_6^3/f_2\pmod{81}$ in generating-function form. We relate the numbers $A_k(n)$ modulo $3$ and $9$ to overpartitions, sums of squares and triangular numbers, give group-action proofs of some of the congruences, and close with several conjectures supported by computation.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Yaqubi, Madjid Mirzavziri

item.title: Linear Cotype Bounds for Nonlinear Spectral Gaps of Scalar Expanders
item.description: arXiv:2611.05649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq 3$, whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue satisfies $\lambda_2(G)\leq (1-\delta)d$, where $0<\delta\leq 1$. We prove that the Poincar\'e constant satisfies $$\gamma(G,\|\cdot\|_X)\lesssim \frac{qCK}{\delta}$$ whenever $X$ is a real Banach space with a $K$-unconditional Schauder basis and cotype $q$ with constant $C$. This constant compares the mean distance over all vertex pairs with the mean distance across edges. For real Banach lattices the bound is $O(qC/\delta)$. The proof estimates where a random walk first leaves each coordinate level set. As a consequence of the bound, if $n$-vertex graphs in a fixed-degree expander family embed with bounded distortion into spaces with bounded $C,K$, then $q$ must grow at least as fast as $\log n$. This order is attained in $\ell_q^n$.
item.dc:creator: Achintya Raya Polavarapu

item.title: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?
item.description: arXiv:2611.06003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We view a $k\times n$ Latin rectangle as $n$ points in the grid $[n]^k$. Each symbol gives one point, whose coordinates are the columns it occupies. The rectangle is balanced when these points are pairwise equidistant in the $\ell_1$ metric. Its imbalance measures the distance from this ideal. We study the minimum imbalance from three sides. Constructively, we use a simulated annealing that moves symbols within rows and only penalises column clashes. Against the reference table of Voboril et al. (2025), it improves 33 of the 51 non-square values for $8\le n\le 13$, by up to 39.4%, and matches the rest. A cheap invariant, the row group, certifies that none of the 33 new rectangles is isotopic to rows of a group table, so the earlier column-swapping local search cannot reach any of them. Exactly, a computer-assisted branch and bound proves that the minimum imbalance of a $3\times 9$ rectangle is $56$. D\'iaz et al. found this value, but its optimality was open. A sharper pruning bound, derived from the identity $I=2\sum(d-t)^+$, reduces the search tree by a factor of $2.4$ to $3.3$ on the instances with $k\ge3$ that we solve. Asymptotically, the minimum imbalance is $\Theta(n^3)$ for every fixed $k$. A pigeonhole argument gives a lower constant of order $k\,4^{-k}$, and random rectangles give an upper constant of order $\sqrt k$. For $k=2$, the limit of $\min I/n^3$ exists, a permuton attains it, and it lies between $4/375$ and $0.1196$. Perfect balance is an $\ell_1$-equilateral problem, so it forces $k=\Omega(n/\log n)$ rows. For $2\times n$ rectangles, single two-minute annealing runs improve five of the seven six-hour MIP upper bounds for $14\le n\le 20$. Finally, the Lean 4 kernel checks every rectangle reported in this paper against a 74-line specification that imports only Lean's core library. We also prove the pigeonhole lower bound in Lean with Mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Li, Vijay Ganesh

item.title: Neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix of graphs: spectral radius bounds and extremal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected graph on at least two vertices, and let $\delta(i)$ be the sum of the degrees of the neighbours of a vertex $i$. The \emph{neighbourhood second Zagreb matrix} $\NF(G)$ has $(i,j)$-entry $\delta(i)\delta(j)$ if $i\sim j$ and $0$ otherwise; its spectral radius is denoted by $\rNF(G)$. We prove that $\rNF(G)\ge\rho(G)^{5}$, where $\rho(G)$ is the adjacency spectral radius, with equality if and only if $G$ is regular or bipartite semiregular, and we use this to show that the same graphs are exactly the extremal graphs of a Berman--Zhang--type upper bound. We sharpen the estimates $\demin^{2}\rho(G)\le\rNF(G)\le\demax^{2}\rho(G)$ by means of the extreme edge weights of $\NF(G)$, give sharp upper bounds in terms of the maximum degree $\dmax$, the maximum neighbourhood degree sum $\demax$, the size $m$ and the clique number $\omega(G)$, and determine the extremal graphs for bipartite graphs and trees. For every connected unicyclic graph $G$ of order $n\ge3$ we prove $32=\rNF(C_n)\le\rNF(G)\le\rNF(\Sp n)$, where $\Sp n$ is the triangle with $n-3$ pendant edges at one vertex, with equality only for $C_n$ and only for $\Sp n$, respectively. Finally, we give bounds in terms of the first Zagreb index and for the neighbourhood second Zagreb energy; for lower energy bounds, the extremal graphs are described completely.
item.dc:creator: Subhendu Chakraborty, Priti Prasanna Mondal

item.title: A Polynomial Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa bound for Eulerian digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In [Combinatorica 1996], Reed, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved Younger's conjecture dating back to 1973 that states that directed cycles have the Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property. Specifically, they showed that every directed graph $D$ contains either $k$ arc-disjoint cycles or a set of at most $f(k)$ arcs that intersect every directed cycle. The function $f$, depending only on $k$, is however notoriously large--in fact, not even elementary. The first improvement on this function was only very recently provided by Hatzel, Kreutzer, Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] who showed that $f$ can be taken to be an exponential tower of height $8$. In this work, we improve this function to $O(k^4)$ in the case where the digraph is Eulerian. This also answers an open question by Wahlstr\"om [Springer Monographs in Mathematics 2018] who asked explicitly when Eulerian digraphs have a polynomial Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property. The only other known result about Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa on Eulerian digraphs is a result from Seymour [Combinatorica 1996] who showed that $f(k)=k$ when the Eulerian digraph admits a linkless embedding in 3-space, and such an equality is not possible for general Eulerian digraphs. We also complement our positive result, by showing that the result of Seymour cannot be extended to give a linear bound ($O(k)$) on general Eulerian digraphs, by showing that even on Eulerian digraphs the lower bound for the Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property is $\Omega(k \log k)$.
item.dc:creator: Esther Galby, Roohani Sharma, Bart van der Steenhoven

item.title: Multiple $q$-zeta values as polynomials in partition multiplicities
item.description: arXiv:2611.06301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Writing multiple $q$-zeta values as sums over partitions, a conjecture of Bachmann, proved by Hirose, Maesaka and Watanabe by means of a recursion, says that polynomials in the parts and multiplicities can be replaced by polynomials in the multiplicities alone. We make this replacement explicit, derive from it bounds on weight and depth that make Bachmann's conjecture effective, and provide a closed formula for the Drop1 operator of Hirose, Maesaka, Seki and Watanabe.
item.dc:creator: Jan-Willem M. van Ittersum

item.title: On the proof of multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2611.06398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we use Wu's method to prove Budur's multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for completeness.
item.dc:creator: Rui Tan, Fanghan Xiang

item.title: Planar Central Configurations of Four Equal Masses: Classification and Morse Indices
item.description: arXiv:2611.06465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the planar central configurations of four equal positive masses under homogeneous interactions with force exponent $A>2$. For $2<A\le 3$, we prove that there are exactly four types of configurations up to similarity and relabeling: the square, the centered equilateral triangle, a unique nontrivial concave kite, and a unique collinear configuration. Combined with known results for $A>3$, this completes the classification for all $A>2$ and gives an affirmative answer to Problem 11 of Albouy, Cabral, and Santos. We also establish the nondegeneracy modulo rotation of these configurations and determine their Morse indices, confirming Hampton's Conjecture 2. Our proofs are based on analytic arguments and exact algebraic calculations.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxiang Huangfu, Huatong Shen

item.title: A $2.81^n$ upper bound on the number of stable matchings
item.description: arXiv:2611.06494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the maximum number ${\rm SM}(n)$ of stable matchings in an instance with $n$ men and $n$ women. Karlin, Oveis Gharan, and Weber (STOC 2018) proved the first single-exponential upper bound; their argument gives ${\rm SM}(n)\le 2^{17n}$ for sufficiently large $n$. Palmer and P\'alv\"olgyi (FOCS 2021) improved this bound to $3.55^n+O(1)$. We prove that ${\rm SM}(n)<2.81^n$. This brings the exponential base closer to $2.28$, the base of the best known lower bound. More precisely, we bound the number of stable matchings in each instance in terms of each person's number of stable partners, where a stable partner is someone matched to that person in at least one stable matching. Our proof assigns each person a weight determined by this number and uses these weights to bound the number of stable matchings by induction.
item.dc:creator: Ebrahim Ghorbani, Matthias Mnich

item.title: Ideals of 2-minors of nearly determinantal matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.06571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce nearly determinantal matrices and study their ideals of $2$-minors. We classify nearly determinantal matrices whose ideals of $2$-minors are prime. Furthermore, we characterize those nearly determinantal matrices whose ideals of $2$-minors are prime and Cohen--Macaulay with linear resolutions.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

item.title: A Sub-$3^n$ Upper Bound on the Number of Stable Matchings
item.description: arXiv:2611.06604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of determining the maximum number of stable matchings. This classical counting problem was posed by Knuth and has been studied for five decades. We obtain a new $2.999^n$ upper bound on the number of stable matchings with $n$ men and $n$ women. This improves the best-known previous result by Palmer and P\'alv\"olgyi. This result gets much closer to the well-known lower bound $\frac{2.28^n}{\text{poly}(n)}$. We refine their entropy-based framework by capturing broader structural relationships among stable matchings. To capture these relationships, we introduce new frameworks, including cones and supports. This establishes the $3.332^n$ bound. We also exploit relationships among local structures and use a charging argument to improve the bound to $2.999^n$.
item.dc:creator: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Hikaru Wada, Masataka Yoneda

item.title: Fixed-Radius Neighbourhoods in Three-Dimensional Unit-Cube Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06747v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Conjecture 4 of Chan, Chang, Gao, Kisfaludi-Bak, Le, and Zheng (SoCG 2026): for every fixed integer $r\ge0$, the radius-$r$ neighbourhoods of a unit-cube graph in $\mathbb{R}^3$ have bounded VC-dimension. Our bound is $2^{2^{O(r)}}$, independent of the number of vertices. The main ingredient is a VC-dimension bound for reachability through arbitrary fixed-length sequences of three-dimensional generalized dominance relations. Its proof uses groups ordered in two coordinates, with neighbouring groups acting as barriers that preserve this invariant when one layer is removed. Combining these bounds with the existing interval-representation framework, we obtain a Las Vegas algorithm that, for every fixed integer $\Delta\ge1$, decides whether a graph given by $n$ cube centres has diameter at most $\Delta$ in expected $O_\Delta(n^{2-\varepsilon_\Delta})$ time, for an explicit constant $\varepsilon_\Delta>0$. Finally, for every integer $r\ge7$, we construct unit-cube graphs with rational centres whose radius-$r$ neighbourhoods have VC-dimension $\Omega(r^3)$.
item.dc:creator: Guangjian Zhang

item.title: Finding full immersions is fixed-parameter tractable in labeled tour graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an $O_H(n^5)$-time algorithm to test whether an $n$-vertex labeled tour graph has a full immersion isomorphic to a labeled tour graph $H$. A labeled tour graph is a connected $4$-regular graph whose edges are labeled by binary vectors of fixed length. To obtain a full immersion, a vertex may be removed only by pairing up its four incident edges and "splitting off" both pairs, summing the labels within each pair. Even for one-bit labels, no polynomial-time algorithm was previously known for arbitrary fixed $H$. Our main tool is of independent interest: we give an algorithmic min-max theorem that, in particular, characterizes the maximum number of odd-length circuits in a rooted circuit decomposition of an Eulerian graph. Our results have implications for vertex-minors, whose study is motivated by applications in quantum networking, connections with graph minor theory, and the goal of developing an irrelevant vertex technique for dense graphs. For vertex-minors, circle graphs play the same role as planar graphs do for graph minors. As a corollary of our main theorem, we obtain a fixed-parameter tractable algorithm for apex-vertex-minor testing in $k$-apex circle graphs. We also prove an irrelevant vertex theorem for such graphs of large rank-width. More broadly, our results are essential to forthcoming work of three of the authors proving a structure theorem for graphs with a forbidden vertex-minor. There, our min-max theorem plays the role of both the algorithmic $A$-paths and Two Paths Theorems.
item.dc:creator: Hadas Barabash, Jim Geelen, Rose McCarty, Caleb McFarland, Paul Wollan

item.title: Monadically Dependent Graph Classes Have Almost Bounded Merge-Width
item.description: arXiv:2611.06804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A graph class $\mathcal{C}$ is monadically dependent if one cannot interpret all graphs in vertex-colored graphs from $\mathcal{C}$ using a fixed formula of first-order logic. We prove that every monadically dependent graph class has almost bounded merge-width, thereby confirming a conjecture of the first and the last author [STOC '25]. Our proof is algorithmic and the witnessing decompositions in the form of merge sequences can be computed in nearly-cubic time. This is a step towards the proof of fixed-parameter tractability of model checking first-order logic on monadically dependent graph classes, which is achieved in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Jan Dreier, Nikolas M\"ahlmann, Micha{\l} Pilipczuk, Szymon Toru\'nczyk

item.title: Boxicity of Power Graphs of Finite Nilpotent Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.06816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The \textit{boxicity} of an undirected graph $\Gamma$, denoted as $\operatorname{box}(\Gamma)$, is the smallest non-negative integer $d$ such that $\Gamma$ can be represented as the intersection graph of axis-parallel rectangular boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The \emph{power graph} of a group $G$, denoted as $\operatorname{Pow}(G)$, is an undirected graph whose vertex set is the group itself, with two elements being adjacent if one is a power of the other. We determine the exact boxicity of power graphs of finite nilpotent groups. For a cyclic group of order $n=\prod_{i=1}^{r}p_i^{e_i}>1$, where the $p_i$ are distinct primes, we prove that its power graph has boxicity $\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i-\max_i e_i$. For a finite nilpotent group $G$, let the number of noncyclic odd Sylow subgroups be denoted by $t(G)$. If $G$ has odd order or if $G$ has a cyclic Sylow $2$-subgroup, then $\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(G))=\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(\mathbb{Z}_{\operatorname{exp}(G)}))+t(G)$, where $\operatorname{exp}(G)$ denotes the \emph{exponent} of a group $G$. When the Sylow $2$-subgroup is noncyclic, and the odd part is nontrivial, the boxicity equals this value or one more, and we characterise precisely when each of these values is attained. The boxicity of power graphs of arbitrary finite groups and the exact boxicity of the comparability graph of the Boolean lattice were posed as open questions in Discrete Mathematics, 349(7):115017, 2026. As a consequence of our results, we answer the latter question completely and the former question partially, by computing the exact boxicity of the power graphs of nilpotent groups.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Jinia Ghosh, Suraj Kumar Sahoo

item.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
item.description: arXiv:2611.06845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors. The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.
item.dc:creator: Itai Benjamini, Mark Braverman, Elad Tzalik, Georgii Zakharov

item.title: Hessenberg character
item.description: arXiv:2611.06852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing. More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology. Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Brosnan, Jaehyun Hong, Donggun Lee

item.title: Deterministic Fault-Tolerant Connectivity Oracles with Subquadratic Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.06857v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fault-tolerant (FT) connectivity oracle for an $n$-vertex graph $G=(V,E)$ determines whether $G- F$ is connected for any query set $F\subseteq E$. When the number of failures is unrestricted, prior constructions exhibited a sharp contrast between randomization and determinism: randomized oracles use only $\widetilde{O}(n)$ space [Duan and Pettie, SICOMP 2020], whereas no deterministic construction was known to improve upon storing $G$ explicitly, requiring $\Theta(n^2)$ bits in the worst case. The promise that $F\subseteq E$ is essential for subquadratic space: allowing arbitrary queries $F\subseteq V\times V$ forces quadratic space. For queries containing at most $f$ failures, Khanna, Konrad, and Putterman [SODA 2027] recently constructed deterministic oracles using $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{f}n)$ space that also report approximate distances with polylogarithmic stretch. Their result improves upon the classical $O(fn)$ space bound for deterministic connectivity oracles [P\u{a}tra\c{s}cu and Thorup, FOCS 2007], but offers no space savings over storing $G$ when $f=\Theta(n^2)$. We present the first deterministic connectivity oracles with subquadratic space for failure sets of unrestricted size, using $\widetilde{O}(n^{7/4})$ space. We also establish the first polynomial separation between deterministic and randomized connectivity oracles, proving that every deterministic oracle requires $\widetilde{\Omega}(n^{3/2})$ bits in the worst case. For queries containing at most $f$ failures, we obtain deterministic connectivity oracles using $\widetilde{O}(f^{2/5}n)$ space, improving the dependence on $f$ in the bound of Khanna et al., and prove a lower bound of $\widetilde{\Omega}(f^{1/4}n)$ bits.
item.dc:creator: Merav Parter, Elad Tzalik

item.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2611.06862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $\Phi(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).
item.dc:creator: Giordano Cotti

item.title: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
item.description: arXiv:2611.06917v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) describe complementary quantum measurements: certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. In dimension six, triples of MUBs are known, but whether a fourth basis could exist remained unresolved for over three decades. OpenAI recently reported a proof that none exists. Here we use the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, to characterize all sets in dimension six. We prove that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix. Since none of them extend to a fourth basis, this also proves that no four MUBs exist. Our proof rests on a new topological result that all order-six complex Hadamard matrices except Tao's form a connected space. Connectedness reduces the classification of triples to finitely many overlapping four-dimensional phase balls. We certify with interval arithmetic that these balls cover the space and for every pair of MUBs represented in a ball, we then determine all third bases that extend it. Dimension six is now the first non-prime-power dimension in which all sets of MUBs are classified.
item.dc:creator: Mateo C\'ardenes Wuttig, Joseph Tindall

item.title: Combinatorics behind discriminants of polynomial systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.02963v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polymatroids provide a suitable combinatorial framework for enumerating components of discriminants of polynomial systems, a generalization of classical discriminants introduced by Gelfand, Kapranov, and Zelevinsky for multivariate polynomials. We explore the relations among polymatroids, their induced matroids, and principal partitions, following works of Fujishige and Narayanan. We obtain a sufficient condition for a polymatroid contraction to commute with taking the induced matroid. We establish a correspondence between different classes of polymatroids and critical values of their principal partitions. Three new conjectures about discriminants of polynomial systems are formulated.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav Pokidkin

item.title: Navigating Posets with Few Maps
item.description: arXiv:2605.20877v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two new parameters for finite posets motivated by the problem of efficiently determining the set of successors of a given element. A plane map of a poset $P=(X,\leq)$ is an injective mapping of $X$ into the Cartesian plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. Given two different points $a$ and $b$ in the plane, we say that $b$ dominates $a$ if $a<b$ coordinatewise. We say that an element $x$ of $P$ is tight in a plane map $\mu$ if the following holds: $x<y$ in $P$ if and only if $\mu(y)$ dominates $\mu(x)$. Note that, by definition, every 2-dimensional poset admits a map such that every element of the poset is tight. For any poset $P$, we define the mapability of $P$, $\mathrm{dmap}(P)$, to be the maximum number of elements that are tight in a single map, and we define the atlas thickness of $P$, $\mathrm{at}(P)$, to be the size of the smallest collection of maps such that every element is tight in at least one map of the collection. We relate these parameters to the classical notions of dimension and width: for every poset $P$, we show that $\mathrm{dim}(P) \le 2\mathrm{at}(P) \le \mathrm{width}(P)+1$. On the other hand, there exists a sequence of posets $(P_n)_{n \ge 1}$ such that the atlas thickness of $P_n$ is doubly exponential in the dimension of $P_n$. On the computational side, we prove that it is NP-complete, for a given poset $P$, to compute the mapability of $P$ and to decide whether $\mathrm{at}(P) \le 2$. In contrast to the latter, we show that computing the mapability of a poset is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the natural parameter.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Felsner, J\k{e}drzej Hodor, Giacomo Ortali, Alexander Wolff

item.title: Optimal defective chromatic separation for clique blowups
item.description: arXiv:2609.17557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Guo, Kang and Zwaneveld conjectured that colouring the \((d+1)\)-clique blowup of a graph with defect \(d\) requires as many colours as colouring the graph properly. Norin and Steiner refuted this, proved that the two chromatic numbers differ by at most a factor of two, and asked for the exact constant; the best separation known was \(11/10\). We prove that the constant is exactly two for every fixed defect \(d\ge 2\). Every rational ratio in \([1,2)\) is attained, by graphs whose clique number and fractional chromatic number equal the defective parameter: the separation is invisible to the standard lower bounds. The engine is an exact transfer theorem: a weighted list-colouring obstruction spread over an arbitrary auxiliary graph yields prescribed defective and ordinary chromatic numbers; Kneser graphs then give sharpness. A 29-vertex graph with defective parameter four and chromatic number five answers Norin's Barbados question at the smallest possible defect and palette.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Lecomte

item.title: The Modular Nash--Williams Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.07034v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nash--Williams's orientation theorem converts undirected edge-connectivity into directed connectivity. We extend it to prescribed outdegrees modulo $q$, whose residues must sum to the number of edges modulo $q$. For integers $q,k\ge1$, every such prescription has a realization with at least $k$ edges in each direction across each nontrivial cut if the graph is $(2q+2k-2)$-edge-connected or contains $q+2k-1$ edge-disjoint spanning trees. The method combines a cycle-space approximation bound with rounding that preserves the imbalance across every cut. Fractional spanning-tree packing gives an exact criterion: every compatible prescription has a strongly connected realization if and only if the fractional packing number exceeds $q$. This yields a polynomial-time recognition test. With no directed connectivity requirement, $q$ disjoint spanning trees suffice, proving Hasanvand's prescribed-residue conjecture. For every odd prime $p$, this proves the conjectured statement that the union of $p$ graphic bases over the field with $p$ elements is an additive basis. For every integer $p\ge5$, the theorem and the counterexamples of Han, Li, Wu and Zhang give the exact edge-connectivity threshold $4p+2$ for a modulo-$(2p+1)$ orientation. We also show that every six-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly below three, as conjectured by Li, Thomassen, Wu and Zhang. For three-flow-critical graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, we improve the previous general bound $m\le4n-10$ to $m\le3n-6$, and to $m\le3n-7$ when $n\ge5$. Further applications include Seymour's six-flow theorem, star decompositions, antisymmetric flows, and signed modular orientations.
item.dc:creator: Amir Jafari

item.title: Recent progress in the construction of Hadamard matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.27175v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Hadamard matrix is a square matrix with entries $\pm 1$ whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Hadamard matrices are conjectured to exist at every order divisible by $4$; for approximately the last twenty years, the smallest open case of this conjecture was order 668. In August 2026, Alp\"oge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle announced Hadamard matrices at the twelve orders below $2000$ at which none was known. In this paper we verify and analyse the claimed matrices. We survey results on the existence of Hadamard matrices and list the $85$ orders up to $10\,000$ at which no Hadamard matrix is currently known. In pursuing this work we constructed Hadamard matrices at sixteen orders that were open in the published literature. We conclude with a list of open problems.
item.dc:creator: Ronan Egan, Ilias Kotsireas, Stephen London, P\'adraig \'O Cath\'ain

item.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We give a short proof that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\lfloor4(n-1)/3\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings.
