We also give bipartite plane graphs showing that the coefficient $4/3$ is best possible under the local hypotheses used in the proof.
item.dc:creator: D\'aniel G\'abor Simon

item.title: The minimum number of wheel-saturating edges
item.description: arXiv:2610.33041v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be an $H$-free graph. A non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called an $H$-saturating edge of $G$ if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. For an integer $p\geq 4$, let $W_p:=K_1\vee C_{p-1}$, and let $F_{p}:=K_1\vee P_{p-1}$. Let $f_H(n,m)$ denote the minimum number of $H$-saturating edges of an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph with exactly $m$ edges, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ denote the Tur{\'a}n number. In this paper, for each fixed integer $k\geq 3$, we determine the exact value of $f_{W_{2k+1}}(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,F_{2k})+1)$ and show that $f_{W_{2k}}(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,F_{2k-1})+1)=\left(\frac{2}{33}+o(1)\right)n^2.$ Moreover, we characterize the corresponding extremal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Xianglei Chen, Changxiang He

item.title: EKR Results for Some Cuspidal Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38472v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_\chi$ be a cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_2(q)$ is $t$-intersecting if $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\{v \in \mathcal{S}_\chi: g_1v = g_2v\} \geqslant t$ for any $g_1, g_2 \in S$. For $q = p^f$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $f \geqslant 2$, and $1 \leqslant t < p$ is an integer, we determine the maximum size of an $t$-intersecting subset when $\chi(-1) = -1$, and when $\chi(-1) = 1$ with $t \leqslant 2$. The proof combines explicit fixed-space dimensions, attaining subgroup constructions, and weighted spectral bounds for normal Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Liao

item.title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41529v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective. In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes. For rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes whose vertices have coordinates that are reciprocals of integers, we show that the resulting numerator is a polynomial and is effective.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Uchiumi

item.title: Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.41668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A proper coloring $\varphi$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable. This improves the maximum average degree bound $18/7$ of Kashima, \v{S}krekovski and Xu, and removes the assumption $g(G)\ge7$ from the $8/3$ theorem of Qi, Song and Cao. We also show that the $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$ list-size bound is best possible for graphs with maximum average degree arbitrarily close to $8/3$ from below. As an immediate consequence, our theorem implies that every planar graph of girth at least $8$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.
item.dc:creator: Huijuan Xu

item.title: Berenstein-Zelevinsky polytopes for type $\mathrm{G}_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.42038v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2001, Berenstein and Zelevinsky presented a polyhedral model for the problem of computing tensor-product multiplicities for semisimple Lie algebras. We provide explicit linear equations and inequalities for Berenstein--Zelevinsky (BZ) polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras. We prove that the denominator of a type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ BZ polytope divides $180$, and that this bound is sharp, while the quasi-period of the Ehrhart quasipolynomial of such a polytope is always a divisor of $6$. We also show that BZ~polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras can fail to satisfy Ehrhart positivity, in contrast to a conjectured property of BZ polytopes for all classical types.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Magnuson, Tyrrell McAllister

item.title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods
item.description: arXiv:2611.00145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode. We further show that adjoint operator splitting methods can be described algebraically through the antipode and the canonical involution of the original method. The resulting framework also yields new combinatorial identities and connects the analysis of geometric numerical integrators with the theory of incidence Hopf algebras.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel A. Barrios de Leon

item.title: On the minimum bisection of random $3$-regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2009.00598v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we give new bounds on the bisection width of random 3-regular graphs on $n$ vertices. The main contribution is a new lower bound of $0.103295n$ based on a first moment method together with a structural analysis of the graph, thereby improving a 27-year-old result of Kostochka and Melnikov. We also give a complementary upper bound of $0.139822n$ by combining a result of Lyons with original combinatorial insights. Developping this approach further, we obtain a non-rigorous improved upper bound with the help of Monte Carlo simulations.
item.dc:creator: Lyuben Lichev, Dieter Mitsche

item.title: Community detection with the Bethe-Hessian
item.description: arXiv:2411.02835v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Bethe-Hessian matrix, introduced by Saade, Krzakala, and Zdeborov\'a (2014), is a Hermitian matrix designed for applying spectral clustering algorithms to sparse networks. Rather than employing a non-symmetric and high-dimensional non-backtracking operator, a spectral method based on the Bethe-Hessian matrix is conjectured to also reach the Kesten-Stigum detection threshold in the sparse stochastic block model (SBM). We provide the first rigorous analysis of the Bethe-Hessian spectral method in the SBM under both the bounded expected degree and the growing degree regimes. Specifically, we demonstrate that: (i) When the expected degree $d\geq 2$, the number of negative outliers of the Bethe-Hessian matrix can consistently estimate the number of blocks above the Kesten-Stigum threshold, thus confirming a conjecture from Saade, Krzakala, and Zdeborov\'a (2014) for $d\geq 2$. (ii) For sufficiently large $d$, its eigenvectors can be used to achieve weak recovery. (iii) As $d\to\infty$, we establish the concentration of the locations of its negative outlier eigenvalues, and weak consistency can be achieved via a spectral method based on the Bethe-Hessian matrix.
item.dc:creator: Ludovic Stephan, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Noncommutative marked surfaces II: tagged triangulations, clusters, and their symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2507.20393v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The aim of the paper is to define noncommutative cluster structure on several algebras ${\mathcal A}$ related to marked surfaces possibly with orbifold points of various orders, which includes noncommutative clusters, i.e., embeddings of a given group $G$ into the multiplicative monoid ${\mathcal A}^\times$ and an action of a certain braid-like group $Br_{\mathcal A}$ by automorphisms of each cluster group in a compatible way. For punctured surfaces we construct new symmetries, noncommutative tagged clusters and establish a noncommutative Laurent Phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Arkady Berenstein, Min Huang, Vladimir Retakh

item.title: Strongly Regular Graphs of Rank Four
item.description: arXiv:2510.25410v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Strongly regular graphs are regular graphs with a constant number of common neighbours between adjacent vertices, and a constant number of common neighbours between non-adjacent vertices. These graphs have been of great interest over the last few decades and often give rise to interesting groups of automorphisms. In this paper we take a reverse approach, and leverage strong classification results on rank four permutation groups to classify the strongly regular graphs which yield such groups as a group of automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: William H. Allen

item.title: Balanced subsets in root systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.11219v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Balanced and well-balanced subsets of the set of positive roots of compact Lie algebras arise naturally in problems related to Hermitian and spin geometry. In this paper we compute the maximal and minimal size of well-balanced subsets in all simple root systems.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Moroianu, Paul Schwahn

item.title: Sharp Bounds on the Eigenvalues of Kikuchi Graphs and Applications to Quantum Max Cut
item.description: arXiv:2605.14994v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the maximum eigenvalue of the (both signed and unsigned) Laplacian of level $k$ Kikuchi graph of any graph $G$ with $m$ edges is at most $m+k$. This confirms four recent conjectures of Apte, Parekh, and Sud. As applications, we obtain that tensor products of one and two qubit product states achieve an approximation ratio of $5/8$ for Quantum Max Cut and $5/7$ for the XY Hamiltonian. Moreover, combining our bounds with the algorithms analyzed by Apte, Parekh, and Sud, yields efficient algorithms achieving an approximation ratio of $0.614$ for Quantum Max Cut and $0.674$ for the XY Hamiltonian. Finally, we also make modest progress on Brouwer's conjecture and improve Lew's bound on the sum of the top-$k$ eigenvalues of a Graph Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Ainesh Bakshi, Arpon Basu, Pravesh Kothari, Anqi Li

item.title: On weighted partial triangulations of convex polygons
item.description: arXiv:2605.21921v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the problem of sampling weighted partial triangulations of a convex polygon with $n+2$ sides. We consider the distribution $\pi_{n,\lambda}$ under which each partial triangulation $\sigma$ is assigned probability proportional to $\lambda^{|\sigma|}$, where $\lambda>0$ is a model parameter and $|\sigma| \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}$ denotes the number of diagonals in $\sigma$. This model belongs to a broad class of weighted geometric partition problems that include lattice triangulations and dyadic tilings, and is closely related to several classical combinatorial structures, including the full triangulations of a convex polygon and the associated Catalan structures. Our main result is a simple exact sampling algorithm for $\pi_{n,\lambda}$ with expected running time $O\big((\min\{n,n\sqrt{\lambda}\}+1)\log n\big)$, which is optimal up to the logarithmic factor.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Blanca, Alexandre Stauffer, Izabella Stuhl

item.title: Pairwise Reflection Symmetry in Frequency Rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2606.28315v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many combinatorial designs ask for equal distribution of given symbols across the entries of a matrix. The paramount examples are Latin squares, where each symbol from $\{1,\dots,n\}$ appears once per row and column of an $n\times n$ matrix. Frequency rectangles extend this to $\lambda n \times \mu n$ matrices with repeated symbols under controlled column and row frequencies. In this more general setting, we examine structural properties of pairwise reflection-symmetry, which requires that, on every pair of columns, each ordered symbol pair $(p,q)$ occurs as often as its reversal $(q,p)$. This order-balance is precisely what makes head-to-head comparisons unbiased, i.e., no symbol gains a systematic advantage from the position it occupies relative to another, a fairness demand arising for instance when scheduling tournaments or laying out comparative trials. Existence of such objects for odd $\lambda$ turns out to be remarkably more subtle than for even $\lambda$. After showing that existence holds also for sufficiently large odd $\lambda$, we initiate the search for the smallest possible value of $\lambda$ in this setting. We obtain the insight that a per-column multiplicity of $\lambda=1$ can be achieved if and only if $n$ is a power of two. We complement the existence results with a direct product construction and add several further observations on the property. Finally, we propose and evaluate a quadratically constrained integer program to computationally search for these objects. The resulting experiments reveal that many of them possess an underlying group-theoretic structure which, as we conjecture, may even be unavoidable in certain settings.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Iurlano, G\"unther R. Raidl

item.title: Optimal Sparsifiers for Abelian Cayley Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.08261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every Cayley graph $\mathcal{G}$ over any finite abelian group $G$, there is a weighted Cayley graph with $O(\log |G|)$ generators that is a spectral sparsifier for $\mathcal{G}$. This bound is optimal. Applying our bound to the group $G = \mathbb{F}_2^n$, yields, as a corollary, $O(n/\varepsilon^2)$-sized code sparsifiers for $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear codes, improving on the work of Khanna, Putterman and Sudan (SODA'24) who obtained a similar result with an additional $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ loss. Our proof is strongly inspired by a recent work of Reis and Rothvoss for the construction of $\ell_1$-sparsifiers. Following their work, the abelian Cayley sparsification problem can be reduced to establishing a lower bound for the volume of a certain natural convex body. This volume bound follows from a short, elementary argument that relies on character symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Arpon Basu, Pravesh K. Kothari, Raghu Meka, Stefan Tudose

item.title: Product sets in sets of returns and positivity of symmetric ergodic averages
item.description: arXiv:2608.02873v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study sets of (measurable) returns in countable groups $G$, namely sets of the form $\{g\in G:\mu(A\cap T_gA)>0\}$ arising from measure-preserving actions. Extending a result of Bergelson, we show that sets of returns in $G\times G$ contain subsets of the form $B\times B$, where $B$ is large with respect to suitable notions of largeness that remain meaningful even for non-amenable groups. As a consequence, if $G$ is amenable, then every sufficiently large subset $A\subseteq G\times G$ satisfies $B\times B\subseteq AA^{-1}$ for some large set $B\subseteq G$. We also investigate when sets of returns in $G$ contain product sets $BB$ with $B$ large. In contrast with the Cartesian-product phenomenon above, this problem is considerably subtler in non-abelian groups and is closely connected to `symmetric correlation functions', namely functions of the form $g\mapsto \mu(T_g^{-1}A\cap T_gA)$. We use this connection to show that, for broad classes of amenable groups - including finitely generated nilpotent groups and certain solvable non-nilpotent groups, every sufficiently large set $A\subseteq G$ contains a large subset $B$ satisfying $BB\subseteq AA^{-1}$. Finally, we establish polynomial analogues of these results for finitely generated nilpotent groups, extending earlier work of Bergelson and Ruzsa.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Bergelson, Sa\'ul Rodr\'iguez-Mart\'in

item.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
item.description: arXiv:2610.31513v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods. In $(p,q,r)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment, each constraint involves at most $p$ variables, each variable occurs in at most $q$ constraints, and each domain has size $r$. Decreasing any of the parameters of $(3,2,2)$ or $(2,3,2)$ yields a problem in which every sequence of improving flips has polynomial length, so both Maximum Constraint Assignment results are tight. All three results settle long-standing open problems. Our proofs build on a common construction idea, which reveals a close connection between the local-search dynamics of the three problems.
item.dc:creator: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy

item.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.36372v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph records the extrema of its iterated basin and hill boundaries. Their unweighted counts need not satisfy Morse inequalities, and the reduction can change homology. We assign multiplicities using the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain every vertex with nonzero local homology. This modified reduction preserves both hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We give explicit formulas in low dimensions and for complete layered graphs. We also construct local Morse numbers for path homology and prove agreement with the reachability construction on complete layered graphs, including those without transitive arrows. Counterexamples distinguish the homology theories and show that local Morse degrees need not equal vertex depths. A comparison with discrete-gradient methods explains the role of auxiliary choices.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II
item.description: arXiv:2610.40571v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We confirm a conjecture of the first author [SODA'26] on a strong form of pseudo-telepathy for Khot's $d$-to-$1$ games: for every $d\geq 4$, every $\epsilon>0$, and every $k\in\mathbb N$, there is a $d$-to-$1$ label-cover game of classical value less than $\epsilon$ that admits a perfect quantum strategy using finite-dimensional shared entanglement with measurement contexts of radius at least $k$. As a consequence, there exist graphs whose quantum chromatic number $\chi_q$ is $3$ and whose classical chromatic number $\chi$ is arbitrarily large. This is the first super-exponential $\chi_q$ vs. $\chi$ gap, and it improves on the exponential lower bounds of Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp [Phys. Rev. Lett. '99], who produced graphs for which $\chi\geq 1.1397^{\chi_q}$, and Lalonde, who recently achieved $\chi\geq 1.1546^{\chi_q}$. To prove the conjecture, we proceed as follows. We start with a ``stretched'' version of the Mermin-Peres magic square, obtained by spacing out its equations and linking them with additional long equation wires. This operation increases the radius of the initial measurement contexts of a perfect quantum strategy for the game, while preserving classical unsatisfiability. We then apply parallel repetition to make the classical value small, and we turn the system into a pseudo-telepathic multi-layered Kneser hypergraph via a PCP construction of Dinur, Guruswami, Khot, and Regev [STOC'03]. Finally, we feed the resulting hypergraph into the reduction of Fei, Minzer, and Wang from hypergraph colouring to $4$-to-$1$ games, we establish quantum completeness of this reduction, and we show that it preserves context radius.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Ciardo, Antoine Mottet

item.title: Well begun is half done: the computation of Eulerian paths
item.description: arXiv:2611.00818v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize the uniform computational strength of finding (one-way or two-way, directed or undirected) Eulerian paths in countable graphs. In the one-way case, for both directed and undirected graphs, this problem is Weihrauch-equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}\times\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$, where $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ is the jump of closed choice on the natural numbers. This refines the proof-theoretic strength of the existence of a one-way Eulerian path given by the reverse mathematics framework. The $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ component comes entirely from the difficulty of choosing a starting vertex: with a valid start prescribed, the problem is equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}$, which also characterizes the degree of the two-way directed/undirected Eulerian path problem. We also study the complexity of orienting the edges of a graph while preserving the existence of a one-way/two-way Eulerian path. In the one-way case, this problem is not computable, and we prove that $\mathsf{lim}_2<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{OrientEP}<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{2}'\sqcap\mathsf{Sort}_2$ and $\mathsf{OrientEP}\not\le_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$. On the other hand, valid orientations are uniformly computable for two-way paths and for one-way paths with a prescribed valid starting vertex.
item.dc:creator: Manlio Valenti

item.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.00864v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.
item.dc:creator: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu
